title: fix(billing): repeat grants and held assets never abort the Stripe webhook transaction (MONEY-WEBHOOK-124, T4)
body:
MONEY-WEBHOOK-124 (agent 124, builder Claude Opus 5.5). T4: Stripe webhook entitlement path.

## Bs fixed (each with a test that fails on main)

**B-WH-1 — a client who pays an overdue renewal after the lockout never gets access back.**
Normal-day story: a client's renewal card declines, the plan locks after the Days 0-9 grace (or Stripe marks it unpaid), the client pays from Stripe's invoice email or the billing portal, Stripe charges the card, and the app stays locked for good while the client keeps being billed every month.
Why: the repeat grant (`invoice.paid` or `customer.subscription.updated` unpaid -> active) re-runs the content fan-out on the webhook transaction. `PurchaseFanoutService.stageCoachNewPurchaseAlert` claimed the coach "new purchase" marker with a plain INSERT; the marker from the first grant already exists, so the INSERT raised a unique violation. The code caught it, but PostgreSQL had already aborted the transaction, so the next statement failed (25P02), the whole delivery rolled back, and every Stripe retry failed the same way. The coach's payout for that invoice never posted either.
Fix: claim with `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), the pattern TrialUsageService already uses in the same transaction.

**B-WH-2 — a returning client whose new plan includes a PDF or video they already hold never gets access.**
Normal-day story: a client comes back months later (or buys a second plan from the same coach) and the plan includes the same welcome PDF; the first payment succeeds on Stripe and the app never unlocks.
Why: `MediaAssetResolver` inserted `ClientAssetGrant` (unique per client + asset) inside the paid-checkout transaction and recovered from P2002 by reading the existing grant, but the read ran on the aborted transaction and failed, on every delivery.
Fix: read the client's existing grant first and reuse it; the INSERT only runs for a new asset.

## Proof
- `test/money-webhook-bulletproof.spec.ts` (new): real `StripeWebhookController` -> `BillingService.handleEvent` -> `CheckoutWebhookHandlerService` -> `PurchaseFanoutService` -> `MediaAssetResolver`, Stripe fixtures, no network, over a database double with PostgreSQL transaction rules (unique indexes raise P2002, a raised error aborts the transaction until rollback, a failed delivery rolls back every write). Covers: lockout recovery by `invoice.paid` (access back, coach paid the exact 4900 cents once, coach not re-alerted), the subscription update arriving first, the returning client's PDF, same event twice = one effect, a delivery failing mid-handler leaves nothing half-written and the retry applies once, cancel at period end keeps access until the subscription ends, signature check (tampered body, missing header and wrong secret refused with 400, nothing written).
- Failing-before on main: ci-lane run https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37519199069 (main f2d2750c + the new spec only): 4 failed / 2 passed, every failure `current transaction is aborted ... (25P02)` on the B-WH-1 / B-WH-2 deliveries. (The subscription-update-first case passed there only because that double returned live row references; reads now return copies as Prisma does.)
- `test/money-webhook-regrant.live.spec.ts` (new, real PostgreSQL in mwb-3-live-tests; added to that job's list in ci.yml): the B-WH-1 delivery commits on a real database.
- Existing doubles that modelled the old `create` + P2002 claim now model `createMany` + skipDuplicates (checkout-hosted-activation-once, checkout-settlement-round5, purchase-fanout-coach-new-purchase); their assertions are unchanged.

## Size
672 changed lines (49 src, 623 tests + 3 ci.yml). No migration, no flag, no lockfile.

## C (no fix)
- C-WH-1 (flag off, not day 1): `CoachFirstPaymentService.tryEmitFirstPayment` uses the same INSERT-then-catch-P2002 on the webhook transaction; with FEATURE_ROMAN_FIRST_PAYMENT on, a hosted-checkout or one-time PaymentSheet payment for a coach who already had a first payment would abort the same way (the native invoice path pre-checks). Keep the flag off until it uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
- C-WH-2 BillingService treats any unique violation raised inside a handler as "already processed" and acknowledges it; after this PR no handler on the day-1 path raises one. C (edge, deferred to 10k clients).
- C (edge, deferred to 10k clients): two first grants of the same asset in the same instant can still race the grant INSERT.
